n: Lactating breast with crowded, milk-filled alveoli

ww.Resting breast lobule: Resting breast lobule has a few small acini with tiny closed lumens, set in dense fibrous stroma and fat. Here the lobules are swollen and crowded with dilated, milk-filled alveoli, and very little stroma is left between them.
ww.Fibroadenoma: Fibroadenoma is a circumscribed nodule of bland, expanded stroma that pushes ducts into ovals or slits. Here the lobular architecture is intact, with many alveoli and little stroma, and there is no stromal nodule.
ww.Apocrine metaplasia: Apocrine metaplasia lines cystic ducts with tall cells that have abundant pink, granular cytoplasm and apical snouts, usually in fibrocystic change. Here swollen lobules throughout the field have clear, vacuolated cytoplasm and pink secretion in the lumens.
ww.Sclerosing adenosis: Sclerosing adenosis is a lobule-centered proliferation of small, distorted acini squeezed by fibrous stroma. Here the alveoli are round, dilated and unsqueezed, and milk-like secretion fills their lumens.

look: Notice that the lobules in the left panel are crowded together and swollen, with very little fat or stroma left between them. The right panel shows why: each alveolus is lined by cuboidal cells with clear, lipid-filled vacuoles, and pink secretion fills the lumen. Almost the whole gland is epithelium, the opposite of a resting breast.
cred: Mikael Häggström, M.D. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons (resized)
findings: Crowded lobules: in the left panel, swollen, closely packed lobules fill the field, separated only by thin pink septa, because estrogen, progesterone and prolactin multiplied the alveoli during pregnancy.

Fat and septa: along the upper left edge, a thin rim of fat and fibrous strands separates the lobules, and a larger duct runs through the central septum. In a resting breast, dense stroma and fat would dominate instead.

Vacuolated alveolar cells: in the right panel, the cuboidal cells lining the alveolus hold clear lipid vacuoles and bulge at the apex. Lipid leaves by apocrine secretion, pinching off wrapped in apical membrane.

Milk in the lumen: in the right panel, pink granular secretion fills the center of the alveolus. Milk proteins such as casein reach it by merocrine secretion, which is exocytosis of secretory vesicles.
